tieuDeEn: Everyone has some talent, but anyone who is lazy stays ignorant: being clever isn't enough – hard work is the heart of learning. Time flies like a bird, so think ahead: when we're older, it will be harder to learn than now.

dichXuoi.en: Everyone is born with some cleverness, but anyone who is lazy will stay ignorant. Being clever isn't enough – hard work is what matters most.

dichXuoi.en: Time flies by like a bird, so we should think ahead and plan. One day when we are older, learning will be harder than it is now.

baiHocEn: Clever but lazy still means ignorant. Hard work is the root of learning. Time flies like a bird – learn while you are young.

en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson thirty-two of “Lên Tám”. Last time she explained how laziness can waste a whole life. Today we'll look more closely at the link between natural cleverness and hard work, and listen to the poet Tản Đà's reminder about how fast time passes. Look at your book and listen.
Who doesn't have good natural ability? But anyone who is lazy stays ignorant; being clever doesn't guarantee success – hard work is what really counts.
Days and months fly by like birds; we should think about it and worry ahead; one day when we're older, it will be harder to learn than today.

The poem gives an honest, fair truth: “tư chất” is each person's natural cleverness. However clever someone is born, if they're too lazy to think or read, they'll still end up knowing little. Being clever doesn't guarantee a good future. The core of learning – its root – is hard work and patience, thinking deeply a little more every day.

Next, the poem describes time vividly: it passes very fast – a day, a year goes by in a flash, like a bird flying across the sky that never comes back. The child in the poem thinks ahead and worries: when we're older, with many family and life responsibilities, our minds won't be as focused and quick, and learning will be much harder. Understand this, and use every day and every hour to study hard while you are young.
